title: Night-Time Sweet Cravings: How to Control Them Without Suffering
intro: Sweet cravings at night are very common, especially when you eat little during the day, you're tired and work is stressful. You don't need to ban sweets. Plan space for them, and make sure you eat enough during the day.

sections.p: Hunger built up from the day, tiredness after work and stress weaken your self-control. Add to that the habit of lepak in front of the TV or scrolling your phone. This is normal, not a sign that you lack willpower.

sections.h: Start with a day where you eat enough
sections.p: A lunch with protein, a moderate amount of rice and vegetables keeps you steadier until the afternoon. Have a small snack around 3-4pm so you don't reach home starving. Many people with bad night cravings actually didn't eat enough during the day.

sections.h: Plan your sweets, don't sneak them
sections.p: Set aside one small serving, for example 2 pieces of kuih, one small slice of cake or a small ice cream cone, an estimated 150-200 kcal. Eat it sitting down, slowly and really enjoy it. When it's planned, there's less guilt too.
Brush your teeth early after dinner as a signal that the kitchen is closed. Drink hot tea with less sugar or no sugar. Keep fruit like banana, papaya or watermelon for a lighter sweet option.

Many women crave more sweets the week before their period. Give yourself a little extra room that week and choose small sizes. If your cravings are very strong and you're worried about hormones, talk to a doctor.

action: Don't keep jars of biscuits or chocolate on the table or in front of the TV, keep them in the cupboard.
Buy sweets in small sizes or individual packs, not family size.
Make sure dinner has protein like chicken, fish, eggs or tofu.
When a craving comes, drink a glass of water and wait 10 minutes. If you still want it, have one small serving.
Set a kitchen closing time, for example 10pm, for 5 nights this week.
myth: Many believe eating sweets at night turns straight into fat. In reality, your total calories for the day and the week matter far more than the time you eat.

faq.q: If I switch white sugar to honey or brown sugar, is it more okay?
faq.a: The calories are about the same. It's still sugar. What helps more is reducing the amount and how often, not just switching the type.

faq.q: I accidentally finished a whole container of biscuits. What now?
faq.a: It's okay, it doesn't erase all your effort so far. Don't punish yourself by not eating tomorrow. Go back to eating as usual and think about what triggered it: hunger, tiredness or stress.

faq.q: Are my sweet cravings because of PCOS or blood sugar problems?
faq.a: Many factors can be involved, and it can't be confirmed without a check-up. If you have PCOS or are worried about your blood sugar, get your doctor's advice for guidance that suits you.
